metadata.name: ioniqx_transfer_restrictions
metadata.description: Token-2022 transfer hook gating RWA transfers on SAS qualified-investor attestations (BUILD.md 2.7)

instructions.name: clear_redemption_marker
docs: Withdraws the authorisation and returns the rent.
The marker is what makes the hook accept a redemption leg, so a notice
that is settled, cancelled or superseded has to take its marker with
it — an authorisation that outlives its notice is a second redemption
nobody asked for.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Receives the marker's rent back.

instructions.name: execute
docs: The hook body. Token-2022 CPIs into it on every transfer of a gated
mint; returning an error aborts the whole transfer atomically.
Read-and-validate only (§2.7 Section 4.5). It writes nothing, emits no
event, and makes no CPI — every account it touches is borrowed
immutably, so there is no reentrancy surface and no per-transfer log
cost. The audit trail for transfers is the Token-2022 transfer itself,
which the Rails chain listener already consumes.

accounts.name: source_token
docs: `mint` with a transfer in flight.

accounts.name: owner
docs: asserted about the token account's own owner, not about this account,
so it is unused — present because the interface passes it.

accounts.name: extra_account_meta_list
docs: the handler; it sits ahead of the config in the wire order, so an
Anchor seeds constraint here could not reach the recorded bump.

accounts.name: sas_program
docs: attestation PDAs can be declared as external PDAs against it.

accounts.name: destination_attestation
docs: `sas::read`.

accounts.name: source_attestation
docs: configured for two-sided gating.

accounts.name: instructions_sysvar
docs: sysvar; read through `load_instruction_at_checked`, which validates the
data it parses.

accounts.name: ptp_counter
docs: The §7704 accumulator. The hook's only write.

accounts.name: redemption_marker
docs: empty account, which is how the hook tells a redemption from a transfer.
When it does exist it is verified as this program's PDA before it is
read.

instructions.name: initialize_extra_account_meta_list
docs: Creates the `ExtraAccountMetaList` PDA for a mint (§2.7 Section 4.2).
Called once per mint, after its offering config exists. Until it exists
every transfer of the mint fails in Token-2022's account resolution,
which is the safe direction: a gated mint that cannot resolve its hook
accounts moves nothing.

accounts.name: extra_account_meta_list
docs: Anchor account — `init` here allocates it and writes no discriminator.
Address is pinned by the seeds, which are the ones
`spl_transfer_hook_interface::get_extra_account_metas_address` derives.

instructions.name: initialize_offering_config
docs: Creates the offering config for a mint and pins its trusted credential,
schema, and acceptance policy.
Gated on the mint authority rather than on whoever calls first. The PDA
address is a pure function of the mint, so an open initializer would let
anyone front-run an issuer and install a permissive policy on their
mint before they configured it.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The issuer. Must hold the mint authority — see
`initialize_offering_config` for why this is not open.

instructions.name: initialize_ptp_counter
docs: Creates the §7704 counter for a mint.
At issuance, because a transfer hook cannot create an account — it has
no payer to sign for rent, and the transaction's fee payer is not among
the accounts the interface hands it. Window rollover is therefore a
reset in place, never a fresh account.
Written for every offering, including the SPV wrappers that never touch
it: the metas list is a property of the program, so every transfer of
every gated mint carries this account, and one that did not exist would
fail account resolution on a transfer the hook was going to allow.

instructions.name: prove_eligibility
docs: Carries an eligibility proof for the hook to find.
A data carrier, deliberately. Token-2022 builds the `Execute` CPI itself
and its data is only the amount, so there is no way to hand the hook a
proof directly; the client prepends this and the hook introspects the
transaction for it.
It validates nothing of consequence. The authoritative check is in
`execute`, against a leaf the hook computes itself from its own mint and
its own view of the token account owner — so a proof supplied here for
the wrong wallet or a fabricated one is not a hole, it simply fails to
reproduce the root when it matters.

instructions.name: publish_eligibility_root
docs: Publishes a new eligible-holder root.
The only field of the config that changes on a schedule. `updated_at`
is supplied by the client rather than read from the cluster clock, so
the lag between computing a roster and landing the transaction counts
against the staleness bound — the conservative direction.

instructions.name: reanchor_ptp_window
docs: Re-anchors the §7704 window, for an issuer whose taxable year is not
the calendar year. Windows step from the epoch in flat days, so moving
it moves every window boundary after it.

instructions.name: set_halted
docs: Halts or resumes transfers for this offering.
Local to this program. `ioniqx-title-compliance` (BUILD.md §2.5) owns
the authoritative halt for the asset itself; setting this does not set
that one.

instructions.name: set_redemption_marker
docs: Marks a holder's next transfer of this mint as the redemption leg.
Written when the holder's notice window opens, not when notice is
given: a marker standing for a whole notice period turns a redemption
gated to a date into one that can happen any time in the weeks before
it. `amount` caps what it authorises, so the notice the holder actually
gave is what constrains the burn.

accounts.name: holder
docs: seed and as the marker's recorded holder.

accounts.name: redemption_marker
docs: `init`, not `init_if_needed`. A holder has one live notice per offering,
so a marker already standing means the previous one was never cleared —
and silently overwriting it is precisely the failure this account exists
to prevent: an authorisation outliving the notice that justified it.
Clearing first is one more instruction and one fewer way to be wrong.

instructions.name: transfer_authority
docs: Hands the offering config to a new authority.

instructions.name: update_policy
docs: Replaces the acceptance policy wholesale. Every field is restated, so a
caller cannot tighten one rule and leave a stale value behind in another.

instructions.name: update_trust
docs: Rotates the trusted credential and/or accepted schema (§2.7 Section 5).
Takes effect on the next transfer with no reinitialization: the metas
account reads these fields when it resolves the attestation address.
Attestations issued under the old credential stop resolving at that
point, which is the intended behaviour — rotation is how a compromised
or retired issuer is cut off.

types.name: EligibilityGate
docs: The roster gate: membership of one offering's eligible set, as a merkle
root the platform republishes as the roster moves.
A second gate, not a replacement for attestation verification. The
attestation is what ioniqx asserts about a *wallet* and carries no mint;
this carries membership of *one offering*.

fields.name: root_updated_at
docs: When the root was computed off chain — sent by the client rather than
taken from the cluster clock, so the lag between computing a roster and
landing the transaction counts against the bound.

fields.name: max_staleness_secs
docs: How stale a root may be before the hook stops trusting it. Without a
bound, a root nobody has refreshed keeps authorising a holder whose
eligibility lapsed between republications.

fields.name: root_enforced
docs: False leaves this segment inert, which is how an offering is
provisioned before any roster exists.

fields.name: mint
docs: The mint this config governs. Also the config PDA's seed.

fields.name: credential
docs: The single trusted SAS credential. Section 5 speaks of trusted
credential*s*, but the address of the attestation the hook reads is
derived from `["attestation", credential, schema, wallet]`, and an
`ExtraAccountMetaList` declares one address per side. Supporting N
issuers would mean N declared slots and N resolutions on every
transfer. One pinned pair, rotatable by the authority, buys the same
trust property at a fraction of the compute.
Rotation does not require re-initializing the metas account: the seeds
read these bytes at resolution time, so changing them changes the
derived address on the next transfer.

fields.name: schema
docs: The single accepted QI schema UID. See `credential`.

fields.name: authority
docs: May change trust configuration and policy. Section 5: "Changing trusted
issuers is an authority-gated admin action, logged."

fields.name: access_control
docs: The `ioniqx-access-control` config this offering belongs to. Recorded
now, enforced later: admin gating moves to a TransferAdmin role read
once BUILD.md §2.1 is implemented. Until then `authority` is the gate.

fields.name: accepted_classes
docs: Bitmask over `qi::investor_class`. Bit 0 (`NONE`) is never valid.

fields.name: min_verification_level
docs: Floor from `qi::verification_level`. A 506(c) offering sets 2.

fields.name: min_schema_version
docs: Inclusive schema-version window this offering accepts.

fields.name: us_person_policy
docs: One of `qi::us_person_policy`.

fields.name: two_sided
docs: Validate the sender's attestation as well as the recipient's. Off by
default: a sender who received tokens through this hook was already
validated on the way in, and two-sided gating doubles the per-transfer
account resolution. Turn it on for offerings where holder eligibility
can lapse mid-hold and outbound transfers must also be blocked.

fields.name: halted
docs: Local trading halt. `ioniqx-title-compliance` (BUILD.md §2.5) owns the
authoritative halt for the asset; this flag is the per-offering switch
the hook can read without a CPI. Halting here does not halt there.

fields.name: max_holding_basis
docs: Recipient balance ceiling in basis points of supply. 0 disables.
This is a *concentration* cap, not the Section 7 holder-*count* cap.
Counting beneficial holders needs a counter PDA the hook would have to
write to on every transfer, and Section 4.5 constrains `Execute` to
read-and-validate. Section 7 itself notes an on-chain holder count is
only an approximation to be reconciled off-chain; the 2,000/500
thresholds are enforced off-chain against the cap table, which is the
record that actually matters for an Exchange Act registration trigger.

fields.name: tradable_after
docs: Unix seconds before which no transfer is permitted. 0 disables.

fields.name: us_seasoning_until
docs: Reg S distribution-compliance period: unix seconds before which
transfers *to US persons* are refused. 0 disables.

fields.name: jurisdiction_count
docs: How many of `allowed_jurisdictions` are meaningful. 0 means no
jurisdiction constraint.

fields.name: allowed_jurisdictions
docs: ISO 3166-1 numeric codes, zero-padded past `jurisdiction_count`.
A fixed array rather than a `Vec`, so the account has no
variable-length member and every field after it sits at a constant
offset. The account was allocated for `MAX_JURISDICTIONS` either way.

fields.name: metas_bump
docs: Bump for this mint's `extra-account-metas` PDA, recorded when that
account is created. `Execute` verifies the metas account with one
`create_program_address` instead of a bump search; the interface fixes
the metas account at wire index 4, ahead of this config at index 5, so
an Anchor `seeds`/`bump` constraint on it cannot reach this field.

fields.name: structure
docs: The offering's tax/vehicle structure, as a rule branch plus parameters.

fields.name: eligibility
docs: The eligible-holder roster gate.

types.name: OfferingPolicy
docs: The policy half of a config update, kept as one argument so a caller cannot
set half the policy and leave the rest at whatever it was — every field is
restated on every update, and validated together.

types.name: PtpCounter
docs: The §7704 accumulator — the hook's only write.
One per mint, created at issuance because a transfer hook cannot create an
account: it has no payer to sign for rent, and the transaction's fee payer
is not among the accounts the interface hands it. Window rollover is
therefore a reset in place, never a fresh account.

fields.name: window_index
docs: Which window `transferred` belongs to. A transfer in a later window
resets the total before adding to it.

fields.name: transferred
docs: Base units moved in that window so far.

types.name: RedemptionMarker
docs: A holder's standing authorisation to run the redemption leg.
Token-2022 calls the hook identically for every transfer, so without this
the hook cannot tell a redemption from an ordinary transfer — and the two
have different rules. Written when the holder's window opens and cleared
after the burn, because an authorisation that outlives its notice is a
second redemption nobody asked for.

fields.name: holder
docs: The wallet whose redemption leg this authorises.

fields.name: amount
docs: The cap. Without it the marker authorises any quantity and the notice
the holder gave stops constraining the burn.

fields.name: settles_on
docs: The date the notice was scheduled to settle.

types.name: StructureBranch
docs: The structure branch — which of the two rule sets this offering runs, and
the parameters that rule set needs.
`direct_member` makes the token holder a partner of the vehicle, which puts
§7704 publicly-traded-partnership exposure in play: interests transferred
in a taxable year are capped, and that cap has to be enforced rather than
merely disclosed. `spv_wrapper` contains that exposure at the SPV boundary,
so its whole branch is zeroed and the hook skips it.

fields.name: model
docs: One of `structure_model`.

fields.name: partner_eligibility_gate
docs: Gate transfers on tax-partner eligibility as well as securities
eligibility. `direct_member` only.

fields.name: ptp_enabled
docs: Enforce the §7704 transfer cap. Must be false for `spv_wrapper`.

fields.name: ptp_window_days
docs: Length of a §7704 window in days. 365 is the taxable year.

fields.name: ptp_max_transfer_basis
docs: Cap on interests transferred per window, in basis points of supply.
200 is the statutory 2%.

fields.name: ptp_window_epoch
docs: Unix seconds the first window opens at — January 1 of the taxable year
the offering opened in. Windows step from here in flat days, which
drifts a little across leap years; immaterial to a cap, and cheaper
than a write every year to stay aligned.

fields.name: notice_period_days
docs: Days of notice a holder must give before redeeming.

fields.name: cycle_len_days
docs: Nominal cycle length. A bound the hook can reason about, not the date.

fields.name: next_valid_redemption_at
docs: The next date a redemption may settle, as unix seconds. Computed off
chain against a real calendar and advanced by the authority each cycle:
a month is not a fixed number of days, and stepping flat days here
would drift the settlement date away from the one holders were told.
